title: Mini sweep: quick inference metrics & sanity sheet
content:
Purpose: one-pager personal runbook / scratch sheet for quick day-to-day micro-sweeps. Not intended for canonical bench — just fast sanity checks before PRs or deploys.

USAGE NOTES:
- Run quick 3-trial sweep when changing batching/kv-cache/quant profiles.
- Log p50/p95 and cost – if p95 regresses > 15% flag in GH issue.
- Keep tests short (20 requests) to save quota; use stable short prompts.

SAMPLE PROMPT USED: 'Summarize the following email in 25 words or less: [email stub]' (fixed seed, fixed token length target ~60)

ASCII TABLE (rows = sequential runs):
Date	Model	Quant	Batch	KV-cache	P50_ms	P95_ms	Tokens/sec	Cost_per_1k_tokens	Pass/fail	Notes
2026-02-18	redwood-v1-7B	fp16	1	ON	45	94	380	$0.42	PASS	baseline (gold)
2026-02-18	redwood-v1-7B	q4_0	1	ON	48	110	360	$0.12	PASS	~+0.04s p50, p95 +16% (watch)
2026-02-19	redwood-v1-7B	q4_0	2	ON	62	145	560	$0.10	FAIL	p95 regression >15% after batching=2
2026-02-20	redwood-v1-7B	q4_0	2	OFF	58	120	530	$0.11	PASS	Turning OFF prefix cache helped p95 (weird)
2026-02-21	llama-2-13B	fp16	1	ON	120	230	240	$1.15	PASS	High cost; for prod only if downstream quality needed
2026-02-23	redwood-v1-7B	q4_1	3	ON	80	190	760	$0.09	PASS	Aggressive batch but p95 still okay with q4_1

Quick observations:
- q4_0 reduces cost ~3-4x vs fp16, but p95 sensitive to small batch increases (1->2).
- Prefix/KV-cache interactions are non-linear; occasionally disabling ON reduces p95 for q4 variants (suspect cache eviction pattern).
- llama-2-13B gives better language quality on edge cases but cost/latency tradeoff huge.

To-dos (short):
- Re-run failing config (2026-02-19) with 50 requests to confirm regression reproducible.
- Add a tiny script to auto-collect p50/p95 + cost per run and push CSV to GH (shortcut).
- Add a tiny column for sequence_length to see sensitivity.

Open questions / hypotheses:
- Is the p95 regression from batching due to kernel fusion limits on q4_0? (check runtime logs)
- Do small sequence_length distributions trigger different kernel paths? Add a short seq-length sweep.

Next quick tests (ranked):
1) q4_0 batch 1/2/4 with seq_len 60/120 (20 requests each) + runtime trace on failing ones.
2) q4_1 batch 2 with KV-cache toggles (ON/OFF) to validate eviction hypothesis.
3) FP16 batch 2 vs q4_0 batch 2 — isolate cause of p95 blip.

Notes-to-self: keep this file light. When results stabilize, move summary + annotated chart to GH under infer-bench/mini-summaries. If repeated p95 issues appear, open INF ticket and CC eng-sre.

Quick links: GH perf test macro: https://github.com/repo/infer-bench/actions (bookmark), trace snippet in slack thread: https://slack.com/archives/C12345/p167...

End of sheet.
